units.summary: The discovered aggregate backend's ReverseProxy now sets FlushInterval to -1, so every write is flushed to the client at once. Responses with a Content-Length were previously buffered, so this changes streaming behavior for all aggregate traffic.
units.headline: Aggregate backend proxy now flushes after every write
units.reason: Changes runtime proxy flushing for all traffic through this backend.
focus: Flushing per write is acceptable for large non-watch responses with Content-Length
Same setting is applied consistently to all proxies

units.summary: The forward backend's ReverseProxy now sets FlushInterval to -1, flushing every write immediately. Responses with a Content-Length were previously buffered, so this changes behavior for all forwarded traffic.
units.headline: Forward backend proxy now flushes after every write
units.reason: Changes runtime proxy flushing for all forwarded traffic.
focus: Flush per write has no performance regression for large list responses
Watch events arrive without delay through this proxy

units.summary: Adds a constant of -1 used as ReverseProxy.FlushInterval, meaning flush after every write. It takes effect through the three proxies that use it, and the comment's claim holds for them.
units.headline: New streamingFlushInterval constant set to -1
units.reason: A constant only; the behavior change is in the proxy units that reference it.

units.summary: The breakers cache now stores *groupBreaker, an alias for gobreaker's TwoStepCircuitBreaker, instead of the one-step breaker. This is a type change that supports reporting outcomes when the status is written.
units.headline: ST fallback breaker cache holds two-step breakers
units.reason: Type change following the alias; semantics are in the breaker.go changes.

units.summary: The LRU for breakers is now created with the groupBreaker element type. It is a type parameter change only.
units.headline: Breaker LRU constructed with groupBreaker type
units.reason: Type parameter change only, matching the struct field.

units.summary: The single-tenant fallback proxy now sets FlushInterval to -1, so each write is flushed immediately instead of relying on ReverseProxy's no-Content-Length heuristic. This affects all ST fallback traffic.
units.headline: ST fallback proxy now flushes after every write
units.reason: Changes runtime proxy flushing for all single-tenant fallback traffic.
focus: Flushing per write is acceptable for non-watch responses
ModifyResponse origin check still runs before any flush

units.summary: The return type changes to *groupBreaker, matching the cache's new element type. The key and locking logic are unchanged.
units.headline: breakerForDestination returns groupBreaker type
units.reason: Signature type change only; callers must use the two-step Allow API, which is covered in the breaker changes.
